A cathedral ruin at dusk, one great window-arch still standing, the tracery holding a burning frame of saffron sky, the nave floor a carpet of nettles dimming into blue-green shadow.
A moorland chapel at blue-hour, its squat tower silvered with damp, the surrounding heath draining of colour, a single weathered cross in the yard catching the ghost of the last faint warmth.
A sea-stack monastery at dawn, connected by a stone causeway the tide has not yet swallowed, the eastern light pale gold on the chapel wall, the surrounding sea breathing slow and iron-grey.

A hamlet in a valley at dusk, gabled windows catching the last warmth, fog already rising from the millpond, the woodsmoke from a dozen hearths braiding into the cool dimming violet air above the rooftops.
A drowned causeway at low tide at dawn, ancient stones emerging from grey estuary water, mist still heavy on the far shore, the pale sky reflected in every still shallow pool along the way.
A gothic bridge over a marsh at blue-hour, its arch doubled in the still water below, the stonework darkening to charcoal, a line of reeds along the bank still holding the last cold amber light.

Standing stones on the dusk moor, their rough faces striped in long amber shadow, the surrounding heath a deep bruised umber, the western sky behind them clearing to a cold luminous band of pale gold.

A winding hollow-way at golden-hour, hawthorn and bare oak arching overhead, the raked low sun turning dead leaves to hammered copper, the lane descending into a bowl of soft, luminous, honey-coloured fog.
A harbour at cold dawn, black fishing boats tilted on wet sand, warehouse gables silhouetted against a sky of bone and pale rose, the water in the channel still pewter-flat and perfectly silent.
A castle on a lake-isle at dusk, its reflection spreading on glassy rose-gold water, the surrounding reeds a fringe of dark amber, the far shore already dissolving into blue-grey evening mist.

A hilltop cemetery at late afternoon in autumn, the yews casting impossibly long shadows across tilted slabs, the grass burning amber between the stones, a low mist gathering in the hollow of the lane below.

A fog-morning ruined abbey, its broken tower wearing a crown of pale gold cloud, every arch trailing wisps of mist, the whole ruin suspended between earth and sky in soft, dissolving, melancholy light.
